chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Hasan al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The menstruating woman should perform ghusl with nine ratls of water.

key_terms.أرطال: Plural of رَطْل (ratl), a traditional unit of weight. One ratl is approximately 450 grams, so nine ratls ≈ 4,050 grams (~4 litres).
key_terms.الطامث: The menstruating woman (from root طَمَثَ meaning to menstruate). A technical jurisprudential term.
key_terms.تغتسل: She performs ghusl — the major ritual purification bath required after menstruation, intercourse, or other states of major ritual impurity (janaba).
key_terms.طهارة: Ritual purity — the state required for prayer and other acts of worship

ai.seo_question: How much water is required for the post-menstrual ghusl according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) gives a specific legal ruling on the minimum amount of water required for the post-menstrual ghusl (ritual bath): nine ratls, equivalent to approximately 4,050 grams or about four litres. This ruling is part of the broader Shia jurisprudential elaboration of ritual purity (tahara), where precise quantities were specified to distinguish obligatory minimums from recommended practices. The audience of this hadith would have been scholars and jurists who needed practical guidance for issuing rulings.
